label: early original-phase k/u/d/v/q/h after 1/v/u/k/m
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at early positions t=1..5. About 80% of activation mass falls at t=2-3, and it never fires at t=0, on the delimiter, or during the copy phase. Which token is input matters most: k is strongest (7x lift), then u, d, v, q and h. It is stronger when the one or two tokens before it come from {1, v, u, k, m}. The largest activations (about 0.95 of max) are on k or u right after prefixes like "1 1", "v 1", "m v 1" or "m m u". It is weak or absent when the earlier tokens are other letters, and weaker on repeated tokens (in_first=0). This looks like a graded, roughly additive mix of current-token, recent-prefix and position effects rather than a crisp rule, so the predicate is only moderately precise. Dev scores: precision 0.39, recall 0.63, F1 0.48, mass recall 0.72.
